notes.meaning: The Lord warns Jerusalem that a solemn time of judgment is coming. Invading enemies will take the city's wealth and divide the stolen goods right in front of the people. God uses even this painful loss to humble and refine His chosen people.

God permits hostile nations to gather and attack the city of Jerusalem. The city is captured, houses are looted, and the people suffer terrible cruelty. Yet even when half the residents are carried away, God spares a remnant so His people are not completely destroyed.

When the city reaches its darkest hour, the Lord Himself steps in to battle against those nations. He fights for His people just as He did during the Exodus and in ancient battles. Believers can rest assured that God never abandons His flock to their enemies.

The Lord appears in mighty power on the Mount of Olives, just east of Jerusalem. As His presence touches the mountain, it tears in two from east to west, forming a huge valley as the slopes move north and south. This miraculous event creates a wide pathway of escape and access for God's people.

differ.view: Jesus will literally and physically place His feet on the Mount of Olives when He returns to reign on earth.
The splitting of the mountain is a symbol of God clearing away all obstacles to bring the Gentiles into the church alongside Jewish believers.

notes.meaning: The people rush into the newly formed valley for safety, running with the same speed their ancestors used during the famous earthquake in King Uzziah's day. Then the Lord arrives in full glory, accompanied by all His holy angels. God's presence brings true comfort and deliverance to those who trust Him.

The regular brightness of the sun and stars fades away on that day, bringing an unusual dimness. In the history of the church, this represents seasons where blessings and trials are mixed together. God's people must hold to faith even when their path seems cloudy and uncertain.

This unique day is fully known only to the Lord, who controls its beginning and end. Although it seems to hang between day and night, brilliant light suddenly breaks through at evening time. God often brings rescue just when His people feel all hope is lost.

Fresh, living water flows continually out from Jerusalem, pouring east into the Dead Sea and west into the Mediterranean Sea. This stream never dries up in the summer heat or freezes in the winter cold. It pictures the saving message of the gospel and the Holy Spirit bringing life and healing across the world.

differ.view: A real, physical river will flow year-round from Jerusalem to the seas during a future thousand-year earthly kingdom.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The living water represents the gospel, and the far larger western sea shows that Gentile believers would greatly outnumber Jewish converts.

notes.meaning: The Lord will be acknowledged as King over the whole earth. All false gods and idols will be put away, and all people will worship the one true God together. True peace comes when God alone reigns in the hearts of His people.

differ.view: Christ will visibly and politically rule all nations from an earthly throne in Jerusalem during a literal millennium.
This describes Christ's spiritual reign through the worldwide spread of the gospel, culminating in the eternal state.

notes.meaning: The rugged land from the northern border at Geba down to Rimmon in the south will be flattened into a plain. Meanwhile, Jerusalem will be lifted up and rebuilt securely within all its ancient borders. This shows how God honors His city and gives His church a visible and exalted place.

People will live safely in Jerusalem without any fear of future destruction. The divine curse is taken away because sin and condemnation have been removed. God's people can rest in the everlasting security He provides.

The Lord sends a severe wasting sickness against the armies that attacked Jerusalem. Their flesh, eyes, and tongues rot away even while they are still standing on their feet. God holds oppressors accountable for their violence and blasphemy against His people.

A sudden panic from the Lord falls upon the attacking armies, throwing them into wild confusion. In their terror, soldiers grab each other and turn their weapons against their own comrades. God often defeats the schemes of the wicked by causing them to destroy themselves.

The people of Judah join the battle at Jerusalem and overcome their attackers. They gather vast amounts of gold, silver, and fine garments left behind by the foreign troops. God restores what was taken from His people and gives them victory over their enemies.

The same plague that strikes the enemy soldiers also falls upon their horses, mules, camels, and donkeys. Every animal in their military camp is wiped out by this judgment. This shows the complete downfall of the invading armies and their instruments of war.

Survivors from the hostile nations turn away from their old hatred and come to worship the Lord of Hosts. They travel year after year to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles, thanking God for His goodness and salvation. God's grace can turn the fiercest enemies into humble, joyful worshippers.

differ.view: Surviving Gentiles will literally travel to Jerusalem each year to celebrate the feast during Christ's thousand-year reign on earth.
The feast is a picture of continuous spiritual worship and joy in the gospel church, since all nations could not literally gather in one city.

notes.meaning: Any nation that refuses to go up to worship the true King will suffer from a lack of rain. Without rain, their lands dry up and their crops fail. When people neglect to worship God, they cut themselves off from the blessings of His grace.

Even a country like Egypt, which depends on its river rather than direct rainfall, will not escape judgment if it refuses to worship. The Lord will strike it with the same drought and famine that fall on other rebellious lands. No nation can live independently of God's sovereign rule.

This punishment applies to Egypt and to every other nation that fails to honor the Lord and keep the feast. Disobedience brings its own painful consequences, while faithful worship brings life and peace. God desires willing obedience from every people on earth.

The sacred words once engraved only on the high priest's golden headband will be written even on the bells of common horses. Everyday cooking pots in the Lord's house will be just as holy as the sacred bowls before the altar. God's holiness will reach into all ordinary things, setting them apart for His glory.

Every ordinary pot throughout Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the Lord, and worshippers will freely use them for their sacred meals. Complete purity will fill the community, and no ungodly person or greedy merchant will ever defile God's house again. Believers are called to live completely consecrated to the Lord in every part of life.

differ.view: Animal sacrifices will be offered in a rebuilt temple during the millennium as memorials of Christ's work rather than to pay for sins.
The sacrifices represent spiritual worship, such as prayers and praise, offered in spirit and truth by the Christian church.
